summary: Updates the IAB Charter (RFC 2850) to be consistent with version 3 of the RFC Editor Model described in RFC 9280. It is a Best Current Practice document.

eli5.summary: The Internet Architecture Board has a charter, like a club's rules. When the RFC job changed, these rules needed a small edit to match.

questions: how did the rfc editor model change the iab charter
what does rfc 9283 change in the iab charter
what is the rfc editor model version 3
subtitle: A small edit to the IAB Charter so it matches version 3 of the RFC Editor Model.

tldr.problem: The IAB Charter in RFC 2850 no longer matched version 3 of the RFC Editor Model, in which the RFC Series is governed by its own mechanisms.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC deletes the phrase "the RFC Editor," from the liaison member list and replaces one sentence about IAB approval of the RFC Editor.
tldr.outcome: The IAB Charter now says the RFC Editor function is defined under the IAB's authority by RFC 9280.

today: RFC 9283 is a Best Current Practice and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 2850.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: In version 3 of the RFC Editor Model defined by RFC 9280, the RFC Series is governed by its own mechanisms. That requires changing the Internet Architecture Board Charter in RFC 2850. That charter also says the RFC Editor appoints a liaison member to the IAB, which is no longer necessary.
sections.eli5: The RFC job is now run a new way, so the club rulebook needed a matching edit.

sections.title: Changed Text
sections.content:
In Section 1.2 of RFC 2850, "Ex-Officio and Liaison members", the phrase "the RFC Editor," is deleted.

In Section 2, under "(d) RFC Series and IANA", the sentence "The IAB must approve the appointment of an organization to act as RFC Editor and the general policy followed by the RFC Editor." is replaced by "The RFC Editor function is defined under the authority of the IAB by [RFC9280]."
sections.eli5: One name comes off a list and one sentence is swapped for a shorter one that points to the new rules.

sections.title: Approval and Security
sections.content: The document is published as an IETF Best Current Practice. It was also approved by the IAB and acknowledged by the Board of Trustees of the Internet Society. It has no IANA actions, and it should not affect the security of the Internet.
sections.eli5: The right groups agreed to the edit, and it does not change how safe the Internet is.

references.text: Internet Architecture Board and B. Carpenter, Ed., "Charter of the Internet Architecture Board (IAB)", BCP 39, RFC 2850, May 2000.
Saint-Andre, P., Ed., "RFC Editor Model (Version 3)", RFC 9280, June 2022.
